chain.label: Unshotpeened taper bore sealed with chlorine-bearing bleached cork
chain.trigger: The chlorine source was traced to a bleached cork installed in the taper bore to retain the lead balance wool; the accident blade taper bore was not shotpeened during production

chain.label: Multiple corrosion pits in the 14RF-9 blade spar taper bore
chain.trigger: the fatigue cracking initiated from several corrosion pits in a line of pits in the taper bore that extended over a distance of about 0.070 inch

caused_by.evidence: corrosion was produced when entrapped moisture reacted with residual chlorine in a bleached cork used to retain the lead wool in the taper bore hole of the propeller

chain.label: 2P resonance stress cycles during ground operation in quartering tailwinds
chain.trigger: The highest ground running peak stress was reported to be about 18,000 psi. This occurred with quartering tailwinds when the propeller passed through the range corresponding to vibration of the blade twice per revolution in the first flat-wise mode

chain.label: Hamilton Standard extended PS960A blending repair without FAA/DER approval and documented it ambiguously
chain.trigger: It was implemented without the knowledge or approval of the FAA or the DER... the memorandum stated only that blades returned as a result of an ultrasonic inspection should be reworked 'per PS960A'

chain.label: Repair technician untrained in recognizing taper bore corrosion
chain.trigger: the technicians at the service centers had not been provided a photograph or model illustrating the appearance of corrosion or cracking in a taper bore... he received approximately 90 hours of additional on-the-job training

chain.label: June 1994 white-light borescope inspection failed to detect the corrosion and crack
chain.trigger: the technician recorded, 'No visible fa[u]lts found, blend rejected area'; the borescope inspection procedure developed and used by Hamilton Standard in June 1994... was inadequate and ineffective

caused_by.evidence: the technician might have expected the type of gross corrosion or cracking more familiar to his automotive background and, thus, failed to realize the significance of corrosion with a more subtle appearance
the corrosion involved in the accident blade was shallow, diffused and more difficult to recognize as corrosion

chain.label: Blend repair applied to an unshotpeened bore without restoring the required surface finish, masking the crack
chain.trigger: the failure to restore the taper bore surface to the original surface finish during the blend repair, as required by PS960A, was a factor that caused the reduction of the ultrasonic indication that allowed the blade to pass the final ultrasonic inspection and to be returned to service

caused_by.evidence: the manner in which the unapproved extension of PS960A was documented and communicated within Hamilton Standard... led to misapplication of the blending repair to unshotpeened blades with unexplained ultrasonic indications
He wrote on the shop traveler, 'No visible fa[u]lts found, blend rejected area,' and used the blending repair procedure set forth in PS960A to remove the ultrasonic indication

chain.label: No recurrent on-wing ultrasonic inspection required for the reworked blade
chain.trigger: Hamilton Standard's failure to recommend, and the FAA's failure to require, repetitive ultrasonic inspections for all propellers... contributed to the accident because the crack in the accident blade would likely have been detected in a recurrent ultrasonic inspection

caused_by.evidence: because no defects were found during the June 7, 1994, borescope inspection, and the blade was marked with 'PS960A'... the blade was exempt from the requirements of AD 95-05-03 for recurrent taper bore ultrasonic inspections

chain.label: Fatigue crack reached critical size and the propeller blade separated in flight at 18,100 feet
chain.trigger: one of the four blades from the left engine propeller separated in flight because a fatigue crack that originated from multiple corrosion pits in the taper bore surface of the blade spar propagated... then reached critical size

caused_by.evidence: the in-flight fatigue fracture and separation of a propeller blade... The fracture was caused by a fatigue crack from multiple corrosion pits
a combination of 2P resonance and GAG cycle stresses initiated the crack from the corrosion pits in the ASA blade and caused the crack to propagate to failure under normal operating conditions
allowing the accident blade to be placed back into service with an existing crack, thus contributing to this accident
it would have received one inspection, and possibly a second, before the crack reached critical size and the blade separated

chain.label: Propeller imbalance overloaded the engine mounts; RGB rotated outboard and distorted the left nacelle
chain.trigger: distortion of the left engine nacelle, causing excessive drag... the RGB was retained on the airplane in an outboard displaced position, as observed by the passengers

caused_by.evidence: The imbalance loads associated with the separated blade on the accident airplane apparently exceeded the design strength of the RGB attachment points

chain.label: Loss of left engine thrust, torque to zero
chain.trigger: several thuds could be heard from the cockpit, and the torque on the left engine decreased to zero

caused_by.evidence: the engines were operating normally during the flight until the loss of a major portion of one propeller blade on the left engine

chain.label: Severely degraded performance; crew unable to arrest a continuing descent
chain.trigger: the combination of the resulting loss of left engine thrust, increased drag from a deformed engine nacelle... degraded airplane performance, preventing the flightcrew from arresting the airplane's descent or making rapid changes in its direction of flight

caused_by.evidence: increased drag from a deformed engine nacelle and the three blades retained in the propeller hub, and added frontal drag from external sheet metal damage
the resulting loss of left engine thrust... The flightcrew then advised air traffic control that they were unable to maintain altitude

chain.label: 800-foot overcast ceiling over the accident site
chain.trigger: A weather observation taken at CTJ, approximately 4 miles from the crash site, reported an 800-foot overcast cloud ceiling just after the accident

chain.label: Off-airport forced landing attempted short of West Georgia Regional Airport
chain.trigger: were vectored by air traffic control toward the West Georgia Regional Airport, Carrollton, Georgia, for an emergency landing

caused_by.evidence: degraded airplane performance... making a forced landing necessary

chain.label: Collision with trees and terrain in a left-wing-down attitude; airplane destroyed by impact and fire
chain.trigger: The airplane continued its descent, passed through some trees, and was destroyed by impact forces with the ground and postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: the airplane then crashed during an emergency landing near Carrollton, Georgia
the cloud ceiling precluded the flightcrew from being able to see the ground and thus to make a more successful forced landing, a situation that contributed to the severity of the accident

chain.label: Eight fatalities and 13 serious injuries, mostly from the fuel-fed postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The captain and four passengers sustained fatal injuries. Three other passengers died of injuries in the following 30 days... the fatally injured passengers succumbed to thermal burns and smoke inhalation

caused_by.evidence: the cabin breakup started at the initial ground impact... Passengers who were unable to escape from the wreckage succumbed to smoke inhalation
